title: SLO grace periods and autoresolve workflow compiler for noisy multi-region signals
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see noise-driven paging from transient upstream latency spikes during inter-region sync and autoscaler churn. These pages are eroding on-call effectiveness and increasing MTTA. Existing mitigations (static cooldowns and coarse SLO thresholds) either mask true incidents or generate long tail noise.

Proposal: Implement a small, composable system that introduces SLO-aware grace windows (per-route, per-region), an adaptive signal scoring pipeline, and a workflow compiler that emits autoresolve and on-call handoff playbooks. The goal is to reduce noisy pages by deferring alerting for transient SLI blips that are unlikely to represent user-visible regression, while still guaranteeing escalation for true degradations and enabling actionable runbooks when pages do fire.

Key ideas: 1) Grace windows: short, parameterized hold periods keyed by (route, region, SLI delta, load class). 2) Signal scoring: combine rate-of-change, maintenance flags, recent rollback/rollout events, and KV-cache miss spikes into a single signal score with tunable thresholds. 3) Workflow compiler: given a signal score and SLO semantics, generate a deterministic on-call workflow (silent notification -> background remediation attempt -> page) and an autoresolve plan that can auto-close alerts if remediation succeeds within the grace window. 4) Simulation harness: backtest policies against 90 days of telemetry to tune FPR/TPR tradeoffs.

Why different from prior work: Instead of one-size-fits-all cooldowns, this system encodes domain knowledge (multi-region cutover, autoscaler events, expected cold-start patterns) into scoring and ties thresholds to SLO tier and customer impact. The workflow compiler outputs audit-friendly, parameterized runbooks to reduce decision friction for pagers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deploy scoring pipeline in canary region and show >=40% reduction in non-actionable pages for routes tagged 'best-effort' over 14 days without an increase in customer-visible error rate. 2) Autoresolve must only close alerts with remediation logs and telemetry proof (KV hit recovery, request latency return to baseline) and must create an audit event. 3) Workflow compiler must produce a human-readable runbook and an automated remediation step that runs in a sandbox namespace and can be toggled per-customer. 4) Rollout knobs available in Console (per-team toggle, SLO-tier override, dry-run mode).
implementation_notes:
- Build a lightweight scoring service (Go) that ingests stream of SLI deltas and contextual events (deployments, autoscaler activity, region failovers).
- Implement grace-window evaluation as a sliding-window finite-state machine to avoid timers explosion.
- Workflow compiler: use templated fragments (notify, background-fix, page, fallback) and a small DSL to compose them. Store compiled playbooks in the runbook store with versioning.
- Telemetry: emit metrics for 'deferred_alerts', 'autoreresolved_alerts', 'manual_escalations', and per-policy false-positive/false-negative counters.
- Backtest harness: python notebooks to run scenarios and produce ROC-style tradeoff tables.
- Configuration: expose per-route YAML with fields: grace_ms, score_thresholds, escalation_sequence, autoresolve_policy.
- Safety: autoresolve must require >=2 independent signals of recovery and a successful dry-run remediation in the sandbox before enabling for production.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit & integration tests + simulation locally. 2) Canary deploy scoring service in us-west-2 for low-SLA routes; enable dry-run mode (produce alerts but do not suppress) for 7 days. 3) Enable suppression in us-west-2 for selected routes with daily review. 4) Expand to one EU region and run A/B test against control region for 14 days. 5) Gradual global rollout with per-team opt-out and Console controls. 6) Post-rollout 30-day review and tuning.
runbook_excerpt: Title: Transient latency spike — SLO grace path
Trigger: scoring_service emits score >= page_threshold and grace window expired
Step 1 (silent): Post correlation context to #oncall and run automated KV-cache refill job in sandbox (script: tools/kv_refill.sh), attach run id.
Step 2 (background-fix): If KV-cache refill returns success and 95th pct latency drops below route baseline within 3m, autoresolve and annotate alert with recovery evidence. Else escalate to on-call.

Step 3 (page): If escalation threshold reached, page primary oncall, include compiled playbook link and last 30m traces. Ensure runbook includes region failover checklist and circuit-breaker toggle commands.
